log.reply:
**Subject: Executive Briefing proposal for Tamarack Instruments (fictional)**

Dear Dana Whitfield,

**Situation**

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client has deployed a customer service chatbot on its support portal, is piloting AI visual inspection on the German production line and plans AI sales forecasting next year. An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded no inventory of AI systems. Your stated objective is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

**What the Briefing covers for Tamarack Instruments**

The Briefing will map the EU AI Act and GDPR to the three use cases. These points are expectations for the Client to verify with counsel, not legal advice. Questions for the room include:
- Whether visual inspection could fall within a high-risk category.
- What transparency the chatbot may owe users.
- How the requirement that customer data stay in the EU applies.

United States developments will appear only as a general landscape item.

The readiness discussion will start from the Client's Piloting maturity and the June 2026 audit finding. We will then outline a governance operating model using the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen). The board-layer reference is AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards). The model rests on three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent and Final Liability rests with the Human.

We will also cover two points of fit:
- Where the requirement to consult the German works council sits in the sequence before any change touches production staff.
- How AI governance can connect to the ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, the ISO 9001 quality management system and the internal audit function.

The Briefing prepares the ground for ISO/IEC 42001 work. It does not deliver or promise certification.

**Logistics and price**

The Executive Briefing runs for two hours, live and virtual, at US$3,000. It is designed for executive leadership and board-level attendees. The audience roles identified are General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors. Session date: Unknown.

**What the Client receives afterward**

The Client receives a follow-up memo. It records the decisions surfaced and our readiness observations. It also sets out three prioritized recommendations, each mapped to a next program option with a proposed timeline.

**Next step**

Please confirm a session date and the attendee list. At intake we would also like to confirm:
- The scope of the ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 systems.
- Whether any EU AI Act risk classification has been carried out for visual inspection.

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026.

Kind regards,

AI Governance Academy

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.

judgment_calls: The word count is about 441, only about 9 under the limit. A scorer who counts URLs, "ISO/IEC" or "US$3,000" differently could land nearer 450, though I think it unlikely to exceed it. The case would then fail on the word limit alone, since K12 is not in play.

"The audience roles identified are..." restates the AUDIENCE_ROLES field. I treated it as a Profile Block fact and not as an inferred attendance relation under Guardrail 6. Another scorer could read it as asserting who attends.
The works council sentence follows from a stated constraint applied to the production line pilot, which scorer guidance v1.14.3 treats as not a new Client fact. I applied that guidance.
K12 is not applicable because the principles are listed by name only and no principle is defined or glossed.
score.reasoning: All seven checklist items are met. The letter is a single Mode A proposal with every required section and a subject line. Duration and price are unaltered. Client facts come from the block or appear as proposed work or intake questions. Framework names carry their URLs. Regulatory points are framed as expectations to verify with counsel, and no certification is promised. The closing line is exact, and I found no em dashes or Oxford commas. The word count is under 450 but close. No fail indicator appears: no invented Client fact, no altered program constant, and no incumbent register, process or control asserted beyond the framework names.
